name: Dhoot Transmission Ltd
tagline: Dominant 2W/3W wiring-harness maker (41% combined share, ~70% in EV 2W/3W) with a real content-per-vehicle tailwind - but a ~Rs 30,000 Cr market cap and ~75x earnings put it outside the 10x/100x thesis
business_overview: Dhoot Transmission manufactures integrated wiring harnesses (~77% of FY26 revenue), plus battery packs, charging solutions, sensors, controllers, EV cord sets and automotive switches, primarily for two- and three-wheeler OEMs (Bajaj, TVS, Honda; Hero and Ather added via the Multilink acquisition). Bajaj is the largest customer at ~32% of revenue. IPO 17 August 2026 at Rs 871; traded ~Rs 1,475 by 31 Aug 2026 (+69%). Promoter Rahul Dhoot (Aurangabad auto-dealership family background). Bain Capital is an equity holder post pre-IPO infusion.
fundamentals_table: ~0.38-0.40 (deleveraging; ~Rs 767 Cr of fresh issue earmarked for debt repayment)
fundamentals_narrative: High-quality franchise: 37.6% share of overall 2W wiring harness, >70% of 3W, 41% combined, and clear EV 2W/3W leadership at ~70% - with a structural content-per-vehicle tailwind as EV harnesses are materially more complex than ICE. FY26 revenue grew 31% to ~Rs 4,525 Cr; PAT grew only 12% to ~Rs 397 Cr (margin/mix and interest/depreciation drag). 3-yr revenue CAGR ~27-29%. Balance sheet is deleveraging with IPO proceeds. The problem for this screen is not quality - it is size and price: ~Rs 30,000 Cr market cap at ~75x trailing earnings on 12% PAT growth.
technical_read: Not pulled (just listed 17 Aug 2026). Trading ~69% above the Rs 871 issue price two weeks post-listing.
sentiment_summary: First-time look at the ValuePickr thread (topic 224039) - a single introductory post by Nisarg-Shah dated 31 Aug 2026 (company/sector primer, financial highlights, market-share and TAM data from the DRHP, customer list, promoter background). No discussion, no second opinion, nothing to escalate. highest_post_number = 1.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users in the thread. Sole poster Nisarg-Shah is not on the trusted list. Discovery came via Step 1 (recency) with a P2 theme keyword hit ('transmission' / auto ancillary).
bse_notes: Not independently checked (listed two weeks). DRHP-sourced figures per the thread: domestic 2/3W wiring-harness TAM ~Rs 7,006 Cr growing ~14% to FY31; EV 2W harness TAM ~Rs 694 Cr growing ~39-41% to FY31. No pledge or adverse item surfaced.

value_chain.position: Tier-1 supplier - wiring harnesses, battery packs, sensors and switches into 2W/3W OEMs (Bajaj, TVS, Honda, Hero, Ather); dominant share leader in its niche
value_chain.bottleneck_node: EV 2W/3W wiring harness (design complexity + OEM qualification) - Dhoot holds ~70% share, so this is the pricing-power node it already controls
value_chain.note: Genuinely well-positioned at the EV-harness bottleneck with a content-per-vehicle tailwind, but the node is already consolidated in Dhoot's favour and the market has priced that in at ~75x. Customer concentration (Bajaj ~32%) is the main structural risk.

bull_case: Dominant, hard-to-dislodge share (41% combined 2W/3W harness, ~70% EV 2W/3W) with high switching costs once designed-in
Structural content-per-vehicle growth as EV harnesses are far more complex than ICE, on top of EV penetration itself
Strong growth record (3-yr revenue CAGR ~27-29%; FY26 revenue +31%) and improving returns (~28% ROCE ex-surplus cash)
Deleveraging with IPO proceeds; Bain Capital on the cap table
Multilink acquisition broadened the customer base to Hero and Ather
bear_case: ~Rs 30,050 Cr market cap - a literal 10x needs ~Rs 3 lakh Cr, which is not a realistic outcome for a 2W/3W harness maker; 100x in 10 years is not remotely on the table
~75x trailing earnings (vs ~45x at IPO, already up 69% post-listing) on only 12% FY26 PAT growth - priced for years of flawless execution
Customer concentration: Bajaj ~32% of revenue; 2W/3W OEM demand is cyclical
PAT growth (12%) lagging revenue growth (31%) in FY26 - operating leverage has not shown up below the EBITDA line yet
Only two weeks listed; no independent track record as a public company, thin float dynamics
verdict_headline: Best-in-class 2W/3W wiring-harness franchise with a real EV content tailwind, but large-cap size and a ~75x multiple put it outside the 10x/100x screen
verdict_reasoning: theme match (P2): Auto ancillaries - the business genuinely fits (EV harness content growth), so the theme tag is earned, but theme fit does not override the return-magnitude gate

Large-cap (~Rs 30,000 Cr) with no specific named management or structural regime change of the large-cap-exception type - EV mix shift is a tailwind, not a governance/regulatory inflection - so thesis_fit is 'neither' on size math
Valuation compounds the problem: ~75x trailing earnings after a 69% post-listing pop, on 12% PAT growth, leaves no margin of safety
Filtered out; conviction Low. Worth a fresh look only if the price corrects materially toward the IPO multiple or if a few public quarters show PAT growth catching up to revenue growth

four_box.note: value_chain explicit: 'Dhoot holds ~70% share, so this is the pricing-power node it already controls' (moat=yes); EV-harness content-per-vehicle is a real tailwind (yes); but large-cap size math applies (tam=no) and '~75x trailing earnings after a 69% post-listing pop... leaves no margin of safety' (valuation=no).
